body:
Found while triaging the CultureMech unresolved residual. Evidence table:
`reports/culturemech_ambiguous_identifiers.tsv` (written by
`scripts/triage_culturemech_residual.py`).

55 CultureMech surface forms (383 recipe mentions) fold onto a MIM label that **two or
more records publish**. CultureMech fails closed on an ambiguous `label_index` row, so
each of these is an unresolvable ingredient — and unlike a plain miss, it cannot be fixed
by adding a spelling, because the question "which record owns this name?" has no answer
yet.

Ranked by affected mentions:

| mentions | identifier set |
|---:|---|
| 141 | `MICRO:0001647` / `NCIT:C75874` (Sea Salt) |
| 95 | `FOODON:03315719` / `mesh:C017721` (Casamino acids) |
| 34 | `MICRO:0000460` + 5 `kgmicrobe.ingredient:*` vitamin solutions |
| 28 | `FOODON:03315719` / `MICRO:0000182` (Pancreatic digest of casein) |
| 19 | `CHEBI:17439` / `CHEBI:176843` (Vitamin B12) |
| 14 | `CHEBI:3312` / `CHEBI:86158` (CaCl2 2H2O) |
| 14 | `CHEBI:91247` / `kgmicrobe.ingredient:l-cysteine_x_hcl_x_h2o_solution` |
| 10 | `CHEBI:31795` / `CHEBI:32599` (MgSO4 7H2O) |
| 5 | `CHEBI:35696` / `kgmicrobe.compound:cocl2_x_2_h2o` / `cocl2_x_4_h2o` |
| 3 | `CHEBI:17909` / `CHEBI:26833` (sulfur) |

These are not all one defect. At least three kinds are mixed here, and they want different
answers:

1. **Duplicate records on one substance** — `Sea Salt`, `Casamino acids`. A merge under the
   `merge-ingredients` skill.
2. **Granularity disagreement** — `CHEBI:17909` (sulfur atom) vs `CHEBI:26833` (elemental
   sulfur); `CHEBI:17439` (cyanocobalamin) vs `CHEBI:176843` (cobalamin). A decision under
   MAPPING_SEMANTICS Section 3, not a merge.
3. **A wrong synonym on a hydrate sibling, which is an identity error rather than an
   ambiguity.** `CoCl2 6H2O` matches records for the **di**- and **tetra**-hydrate, so
   those records carry a hexahydrate spelling they do not denote. Same shape for
   `CaCl2 2H2O` against `CHEBI:3312`, which is anhydrous calcium chloride. Hydration state
   is identity (MAPPING_SEMANTICS Section 3): these synonyms should be removed regardless
   of how the ambiguity is resolved.

Kind 3 is the one worth doing first -- it is a wrong claim now being published, whereas
kinds 1 and 2 are unresolved questions.

Not addressed in the grounding PR that found this: resolving these needs per-family
judgement, and the PR deliberately skips every shared identifier rather than picking an
owner arbitrarily.

comments.body: Evidence table has moved: it is now tracked at `mappings/culturemech_ambiguous_identifiers.tsv` rather than the gitignored `reports/` path this issue originally cited (#512).

Re-measured while bumping CultureMech's MIM pin (CultureMech#415). Two updates:
the count has grown, and there is now a concrete downstream consequence.

## Now 26 identifier sets, 60 records

Recounted this session over `data/ingredients/mapped/*.yaml` with
`mapping_status: MAPPED`:

```
MAPPED records scanned : 2624
distinct identifiers   : 2590
identifiers with >1 rec: 26      (was 25)
records involved       : 60
```

## The hydration-state subset is the serious half

The sets split into two kinds. Benign duplicates that simply want merging:

| identifier | records |
|---|---|
| `FOODON:03315720` | Phytone, Soya peptone, Soy peptone, Soya pepton |
| `MICRO:0000182` | Tryptone peptone, Bacto-tryptone, Tryptone |
| `MICRO:0000193` | Bacto brain heart infusion, Brain heart infusion, Brain heart infusion broth |
| `MICRO:0001363` | Liver extract concentrate, Liver extract, Liver extract infusion |

And sets where records denoting **chemically distinct substances** share one
identifier, which `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` §3 forbids — hydrates are not
interchangeable with the anhydrous or generic parent:

| identifier | real ChEBI label | records claiming it |
|---|---|---|
| `CHEBI:75832` | iron(2+) sulfate **(anhydrous)** | `FeSO4`, `FeSO4 x 5 H2O`, `FeSO4 x 6 H2O` |
| `CHEBI:23414` | — | `CuSO4`, `CuSO4 x 2 H2O`, `CuSO4 x 4 H2O` |
| `CHEBI:32599` | magnesium sulfate | `Magnesium sulfate`, `MgSO4 x 6 H2O` |
| `CHEBI:86360` | manganese(II) sulfate | `MnSO4`, `MnSO4 x 7 H2O` |
| `CHEBI:86477` | — | `Na2SO3`, `Na2SO3 x 5 H2O` |
| `CHEBI:29377` | sodium carbonate | `Na2CO3` (SINGLE_INGREDIENT), `Sodium carbonate solution` (**STOCK_SOLUTION**) |

`CHEBI:29377` is the odd one out and arguably the worst: it puts a single
ingredient and a stock solution — different `ingredient_type` — on one
identifier.

## Why it now matters downstream

`docs/data/label_index.csv` collapses to one row per label, so when several
records claim an identifier the published `preferred_term` is whichever record
wins. That winner **changed between pins**, with no curation intent behind the
change. Bumping CultureMech from `82694054f5` to `9f09e4fb97` moved nine labels'
`preferred_term` while every identifier stayed put:

```
FeSO .7H O            CHEBI:75832  FeSO4              -> FeSO4 x 6 H2O
MgSO4 × 7 H2O         CHEBI:32599  Magnesium sulfate  -> MgSO4 x 6 H2O
MgSO4•7H2O(CAS: ...)  CHEBI:31795  MgSO4 x 7 H2O      -> MgSO4·H2O
MnSO4 x n H2O         CHEBI:86360  MnSO4              -> MnSO4 x 7 H2O
Na2CO3 anhydrous      CHEBI:29377  Na2CO3             -> Sodium carbonate solution
```

Several of those are wrong against the identifier's own ChEBI label — `CHEBI:75832`
is explicitly *anhydrous* yet now publishes "FeSO4 x 6 H2O", and "Na2CO3 anhydrous"
now publishes "Sodium carbonate solution".

CultureMech's `kgx_export.py:340-346` uses `preferred_term` as a KG node `name`
**and**, through `_create_solution_id`, as a node **id**. So an unstable
`preferred_term` becomes unstable KG node identity — node ids that change between
builds for no curation reason. That makes this a blocker for the KGX step rather
than a tidiness issue.

Not fixed in CultureMech#415: that PR only advances the pin, and no identifier
moves in it, so it neither causes nor worsens this.

A measurement from the #138 builder fix (culturebotai-claw#354) that belongs
here rather than in a new issue, because it is this defect seen from the
resolver's side.

`build_unified_ingredient_mapping.py` resolves each CultureMech ingredient
name two ways — by CultureMech's `term.id` against MIM's identifier index, and
by the normalised name against MIM's name/synonym index — and takes the
term-id hit first. On the 2026-09-06 baseline (CultureMech `c85c37080b`, MIM
`main`):

```
rows where both lookups hit a MIM record        1,590
...and they hit DIFFERENT records                 189
```

Every high-occurrence case I looked at is the name index collapsing a
hydrate spelling onto the generic record:

| name | term.id → record | name → record | occ |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `MgSO4 x 7 H2O` | `CHEBI:31795` heptahydrate | `CHEBI:32599` magnesium sulfate | 3,219 |
| `CaCl2 x 2 H2O` | `CHEBI:86158` dihydrate | `CHEBI:3312` calcium chloride | 3,310 |
| `FeSO4 x 7 H2O` | `CHEBI:75836` heptahydrate | `CHEBI:75832` anhydrous | 1,798 |
| `NiCl2 x 6 H2O` | `CHEBI:34887` | `CHEBI:53542` | 2,597 |
| `Na2MoO4 x 2 H2O` | `CHEBI:75213` | `CHEBI:75215` | 3,035 |

That is, a hydrate surface form is reachable as a synonym on the *generic*
record as well as being the preferred term of the hydrate record — the
"same label under two or more records" this issue names, and a
MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 violation on the name-index side. The resolver's
term-first order is currently what keeps the published row correct; I went in
expecting that order to be a defect and the numbers say the reverse, so I am
recording it and not changing it.

Not all 189 will be this shape — `Vitamin B12` (`CHEBI:176843` vs
`CHEBI:17439`) and `KH2PO4` (`CHEBI:63036` vs `CHEBI:32583`) need a look
rather than a rule — but the hydrate cases alone are the bulk of the
occurrences.

title: 25 identifier sets publish the same ingredient label under two or more records
